correctness.rationale: The direct product K_a×K_r (adjacency when both coordinates differ) has diameter two. A subset with no selected geodesic triple induces disjoint cliques. Classifying selected configurations into row, column, transversal clique, and 2-by-2 rectangle yields p_k=a*C(r,k)+r*C(a,k)+(r)_k*C(a,k)+C(a,2)C(r,2)C(4,k) for k>=3, agreeing with the 2026 corrected PRIOR enumerator; p0=1,p1=ar,p2=C(ar,2). For a>=5,r>=2a+4, check strict p0<...<p_a, explicitly absorbing rectangle corrections at 3/4. Beyond a the remaining a*C(r,k) forms a binomial tail with p_(a+2)>p_(a+1). The single junction has (p_(a+1)-p_a)/(r)_a=(r-2a-1)/K-1-1/[(r-1)...(r-a+1)], K=(a+1)!/a. Its integer sign changes precisely between r=2a+1+K and r=2a+2+K. Hence full unimodality exactly at/above R(a)=2a+2+K, while below p_a>p_(a+1)<p_(a+2). Independent geodesic subgraph enumeration matched for 3×3,3×4,4×3; exact boundary signs verified a=5..9 (R=156,854,5776,45378,403220). The infinite theorem relies on coefficient inequalities, not those samples.
residual_risks: Requires a>=5 and r>=2a+4; earlier parameter regions not classified. Published corrected coefficient formula is a necessary prior theorem.
Small direct subset tests and finite threshold checks are not an all-parameter proof; the displayed tail and initial-segment inequalities supply the all-parameter step.
